vectors.author: vector-author-b-5.2
vectors._scenario: RAISE_UNINTERRUPTED. Clear-down, then Hopper_Level_High true and Shredder_Run_Fwd_FB true from the start of the scenario, both held for 75 s, no FaultReset. A correct block raises the alarm at 60 s of accrual.
vectors._observability: Sampled over the last 10 s of the scenario (429 scans at 23.33 ms, ~50x the section 12a floor and ~4.5x the largest poll gap ever measured). A raised alarm is level-persistent and nothing in this scenario can clear it, so one late sample is decisive for occurrence AND for persistence - which is why a one-scan pulse implementation fails here rather than passing a bare latch.
vectors.settlingCondition: HopperBlockedAlarm and HopperBlockedInhibit both unchanged across 43 consecutive observed scans (1.0 s at comp=1) ending at the close of the observation window, with the stimulus model's last commanded transition at least 429 scans earlier. The completion flag is deliberately NOT part of this condition.

blacklist.reason: the stimulus model drives Hopper_Level_High and the shredder running feedbacks, which this block also consumes (register Provenance section, reuse-first result). Running it concurrently means the test's stimulus is driving the plant's own sequencer - coupling through plant-model state that the reference graph does not see, which is precisely what section 7 puts on the blacklist.

uses hopper-high as an instantaneous auto-mode cycle trigger (register Provenance section), so the stimulus model's hopper profile commands pusher cycles as a side effect. Same plant-model coupling; the reference graph sees a shared READ and does not treat it as a conflict.

assertedBehaviours: hopper-level-high discrete sensor held true for a commanded duration
shredder running feedback, forward or reverse, held for a commanded duration
vectors.kills: An implementation that never writes HopperBlockedAlarm at all (the inhibit is wired and the alarm coil is missing), or whose persistence timer can never elapse - preset in the wrong units (T#60M for T#60S), the timer's IN never true, or the alarm driven from a condition the scenario never satisfies. Any of those reads false at 75 s of continuous high-and-running. It also kills a momentary-pulse alarm, because the observation is a late sample rather than an occurrence latch. *** IT DOES NOT KILL AN ALARM THAT RAISES EARLY *** - no assertion in the enumeration forbids that; see the decomposition dispute in the .md.

vectors._scenario: PAUSE_AND_RESUME. Clear-down, then: 0-40 s hopper high + running (40 s accrued); 40-70 s both run feedbacks false, hopper STILL HIGH (NEW-HBA-01 freeze, AR-HBA-06 does not apply because the hopper never reads low); 70-105 s running again, hopper still high. Cumulative high-and-running reaches 60 s at t=90 s, so a correct block raises there.
vectors._observability: Sampled over 95-105 s, which is 5 s after the correct raise and 25 s before the earliest raise a reset-on-stop implementation could manage (t=130 s). The margin either side is 5 s and 25 s against a floor of ~0.2 s.

vectors.kills: *** THE RESET-ON-STOP DEFECT. *** The accumulated persistence time is DISCARDED on loss of running rather than frozen, so accrual restarts at t=70 s and the threshold is not reached until t=130 s - past the end of the scenario, so the sample reads false. This is the defect the enumeration method document records as the one that survived a merged reading of REQ-HBA-001, and it is the reason 001 has four assertions and not three. VB-HBA-001 stays green against it.

vectors._addedAt: Enumeration issue 5. This assertion exists because this author's decomposition dispute was upheld as AR-HBA-13 — REQ-HBA-002 was TITLED 'No alarm below threshold' while AR-HBA-04 had narrowed its text to the debounced-clear case, so an under-scaled preset left all 25 earlier assertions true. This vector is limb 1's alarm half. VB-HBA-027 is the inhibit half and *** THE TWO ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED ***: see its note.
vectors._scenario: RAISE_UNINTERRUPTED - byte-for-byte the profile VB-HBA-001 and VB-HBA-002 run, which is the point: the same stimulus, a different question asked of it. Clear-down (which establishes 'no FaultReset since the accumulated persistence time was last zero' and starts the first uninterrupted episode), then Hopper_Level_High true and Shredder_Run_Fwd_FB true, both held for 75 s, no reset and no hopper-low at any point. Accumulated time therefore equals elapsed time from the episode start, which is what lets a wall-clock arming window express a claim about ACCUMULATED time.
vectors._boundUsed: *** THE PERSISTENCE THRESHOLD IS TAKEN FROM AR-HBA-03's BOUNDS TABLE: T#60S (Q-HBA-01, owner), which at the loaded scan period of 23.33 ms is 2572 scans. THE BLOCK'S OWN PRESET IS NOT READ, NOT KNOWN TO THIS AUTHOR, AND DOES NOT APPEAR ANYWHERE IN THIS VECTOR. *** The armed window closes at 58 s = 2486 scans, i.e. 2 s (86 scans) BELOW the specified threshold, and that 2 s is margin for scan jitter and for the copy layer running one scan ahead of the block (contract 9.4). Sensitivity that follows, stated rather than implied: this vector catches any effective threshold SHORTER THAN 58 s - an under-scale of more than 3.3% - and a preset between 58 s and 60 s escapes it. *** AND THE FIELD YOU ARE READING IS INVISIBLE TO THE GATE: see the finding on AMB-19 in the .md. ***
vectors._observability: *** THE LATCH IS THE INSTRUMENT AND NOTHING ELSE WOULD DO. *** The claim is 'does not assert AT ANY POINT before the threshold', and a sample answers only 'was it true when we looked' - a block asserting at 45 s and a block asserting at 60 s look identical to any sample taken outside the moment. A latch armed over 1-58 s catches an assertion anywhere in those 57 s and cannot fall in a poll gap. The assertion is a WHEN, so Latched is admissible and so is the second expectation. THE SECOND EXPECTATION IS A POSITIVE CONTROL AND IS NOT DECORATION: without it a block whose alarm output is dead passes this prohibition trivially, and the vector would be measuring uptime. It samples 65-75 s expecting true, so the vector reads as one statement - not before 58 s, but yes by 65 s - which is the threshold pinned from both sides inside one test. Arming starts at 1 s so the clear-down, which legitimately clears an alarm with a reset, is outside the window.
vectors.settlingCondition: HopperBlockedAlarm and HopperBlockedInhibit both unchanged across 43 consecutive observed scans (1.0 s at comp=1) ending at the close of the sampled window, with the stimulus model's last commanded transition at least 2443 scans earlier; the latched evidence cannot change once its arming window has closed at 58 s. The completion flag is deliberately NOT part of this condition.

The other side of the boundary - an OVER-scaled preset, exactly as invisible under the old reading - is killed by VB-HBA-001, whose scenario ends at 75 s and whose 65-75 s sample reads false against any threshold longer than 75 s. vectors._notMergedWithVB026: *** THESE TWO ARE NOT ONE VECTOR, AND THE SHARED STIMULUS IS PRECISELY WHY IT WOULD BE TEMPTING. *** An under-scaled preset asserts BOTH outputs early, and REQ-HBA-008's two tracking assertions stay TRUE throughout, because the outputs still AGREE - a simultaneity claim is satisfied by a synchronised error. So VB-HBA-024 and VB-HBA-025 are green against a block that raises both outputs at 45 s, and nothing in the enumeration covers the inhibit half except this assertion. A single vector observing only the alarm would leave THE OPERATIONALLY WORSE HALF untested: the inhibit is the output that stops the plant, so an early inhibit stops a plant that is not blocked. AMB-14 does not apply to either of them - both are single-signal claims - so there is no co-signal to fold in and no excuse for one vector.
vectors._scenario: RAISE_UNINTERRUPTED, the same profile and the same arming as VB-HBA-026. Identical stimulus, different output observed.
vectors._boundUsed: *** AR-HBA-03's BOUNDS TABLE: persistence threshold T#60S (Q-HBA-01, owner) = 2572 scans at 23.33 ms. THE BLOCK'S OWN PRESET IS NOT READ AND APPEARS NOWHERE IN THIS VECTOR. *** Armed window closes at 58 s = 2486 scans, 2 s below the specified threshold as margin. Catches any effective threshold shorter than 58 s; a preset between 58 s and 60 s escapes. Same invisibility to the gate as VB-HBA-026 - see the AMB-19 finding in the .md.
vectors._observability: A NEVER, so no expectation may be sampled (F-3) - and a latch is what this claim wants anyway: an assertion anywhere in the armed 1-58 s window sets it, and a latch cannot fall in a poll gap. *** AND F-3 COSTS THIS VECTOR ITS POSITIVE CONTROL, WHICH IS DECLARED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. *** VB-HBA-026 can carry a sampled 'yes by 65 s' beside its latched 'no before 58 s' because it cites a WHEN; this vector cannot, because sampling is refused for the whole vector once the form is Never, and a second latch on the same signal in the same vector would need a second arming window the copy layer does not provide. So IN ISOLATION this vector is satisfied vacuously by a dead inhibit output. It is non-vacuous AS A SET: VB-HBA-002 proves the same output does assert at the threshold, and VB-HBA-024 proves it holds while the alarm is up. A reader who takes this vector's green on its own has read it wrongly.
